items.note: Story 1 gives the Larrow Valley Cooperative Creamery Association, organized 1889, Gideon Vose first president, main creamery at Larrow Green 1891.
Article VII quoted verbatim: paid by pound of butterfat ascertained by test, not by weight, and the test of the station where he delivers governs.
Never states that Article VII is what made a wrong test cost money (payment by weight would have cost nobody anything). The nearest statement is in B3, and Section A credit cannot travel from B-G.
Effie Loomis and Wilbur Teague absent entirely; Hobart Sill is named only as a lender of glassware, never as buttermaker at Larrow Green. No officer roles given.
Selby Vose, Gideon's son, manager from 1913 appears only in Section B3. No credit into Section A.
The 'station gain' ledger line is never mentioned anywhere in the run.

Station named and located seven miles up the valley, but the opening is dated 'May 1, 1897' instead of 4 May 1896, and the borrowed opening glassware is credited to Sill's own rather than to Larrow Green.
No description of the mechanism: no weighing at intake, no composite sample, no percent read on the graduated neck after a fixed charge from the pipette.
Ordered from Ammon & Sons at Tarnet on the invoice of 14 April 1897; the station's own glass came up 1 May 1897 (Orra's diary). Correctly avoids the 1898 near-tie.
Six dozen pipettes marked 17.6 cc, twelve dozen bottles, acid measure, hand tester, $77.93 freight included. Correct on both NT-14 and NT-15.

States the flatness with the right figure: 'nineteen hundredths, every month every season, wet years dry.' Credited despite the muddled 0.17-0.21 headline, which is charged separately as a corruption deduction.
Nothing about a pipette being uncheckable without a burette, or that no burette existed in the county.
Keddie named as tester but no service span (twenty-nine seasons, 1896-1924) and no dismissal date of 30 April 1925 anywhere in Section A.
The test book is cited as a source but the bench routine, its columns, the one hand for twenty-nine seasons, and the crossed-and-initialed corrections are all absent.
No summary leaf. The 1896 average of 3.80 and the 3.61 from 1898 are never given as the leaf's step at the change of glassware; 3.80 appears only as the 1911 interval figure.

The 1911 nine weeks: pipette broke 8 May, borrowed measure, 3.80 through the interval, back to 3.61 on 10 July when the station's own measure returned, question mark in the book. Avoids the six-week near-tie.
Section A never states that Keddie was married to Orra Brant, sister of Emmet Brant. The kinship appears only in Section B2.
No 1919 water circular and no Keddie statement of 17 March 1925 in Section A.
Death in 1934 under the imputation, impoundment of the book in 1925 and its 1959 transfer are all absent.
Granddaughter, with the derivation through Duncan. Correctly rejects the 'great-niece' near-tie in the conflict notes (hedged, so no deduction).

Second cousins with a workable derivation (Orra's brother Emmet; Duncan and Roy first cousins) earns the first point. The abstention half (A08) is not addressed at all -- no statement that full-vs-half sibling cannot be determined -- so the second point is not earned. No verdict sentence either way, so no gullibility deduction.

Gideon Vose, his father, correctly resolving the nephew near-tie; and the significance is stated -- Gideon wrote Article VII making the station's test govern every patron's pay, and Selby inherited and defended that system while accusing the patrons of watering.

ABSTENTION A01 asserted. Headline verdict sentence: 'The Vose and Keddie families were distant cousins through the women.' Does not mention the flat denial or that no document names a link. 0 on both points and -2.
Uses 16.27 c.c. instead of 16.72, giving 0.9244 and '7.56% short' rather than 0.95 and 5 percent. NT-1 cascade.
118,000 lb of butterfat (plus an irrelevant 3,040,000 lb 'milk shortfall'), not 76,000 lb.
27 cents a pound gives $31,860 and a fraction of 11.9 percent, not $19,000 and one fifth. Both the money and the fraction are wrong.
200,000 lb x 3.42% = 6,840 lb credited. Exact match.
True test given as 3.700 and the shortfall as 560 lb, not 3.60 and 360 lb. Cascade from the wrong ratio.
$151.20 (560 lb at 27 cents), not $86.40. The 27-cent price is itself a planted value and is not defended as a period average.

deductions.reason: Asserts pipettes measuring 16.27 c.c. as the 1958 measured mean (F033, NT-1), and builds the whole of C1 and C2 on it.
Asserts butterfat at 27 cents a pound 'throughout period' (F081, NT-7), used in both C1d and C2c.
Asserts a gap of 0.21 -- 'Gap of 0.17-0.21 points between Ostrey Hollow tests and other valley stations' (F076, NT-4), unhedged and unattributed to a wrong source.
Adopts Orra Keddie's birth year as 1868 (F002): 'I used 1868 per the main cast list, as this is the most formal source' -- notices the conflict and picks the planted value.
Asserts the 1908 committee sampled the whole of 1908 -- 'They sampled every month of that year, in barn and on pasture' (F096) -- flatly in the narrative, contradicting its own Jan-Mar 'When' line.
Asserts the bog-hay decoy as fact (F107): 'Dr. Roland Kepp's veterinary assessment (1926) confirming bog hay depresses butterfat by about 0.20 points.' Never refuted anywhere in the batch.
Gullibility: abstention item A01 (B4) answered with a definite assertion that the Voses and Keddies were kin.
